lots.working: Keep: this is a bundle, so I used the sum of each visible title's lower-quartile loose sale price. The absolute lowest sales are often lot breakups or damaged carts. US$76.16 x 1.4383 = AUD 109.5, / 1.198 = 91.4, rounded down to $90 hammer ($107.82 all-in). Banjo-Kazooie is left out until a cart is confirmed. Flip: likely resale is the sum of medians, AUD 157.1. Less eBay fees of about 13% (AUD 20.4) and about AUD 15 outbound postage, that leaves AUD 121.7. Divided by 2.396 = 50.8, rounded down to $50 hammer. If a genuine Banjo cart is confirmed: keep is about $120 hammer ((109.5 + 21.3) / 1.198) and flip about $60 ((183 x 0.87 - 15) / 2.396).

lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD: dated US eBay sales shown on PriceCharting, new in box, last 24 months. No UNSOLD or ASKING entries were kept. lots.working: Keep: lowest new-in-box sale for each figure in the last 24 months, in USD: Batman 4.99, Beast Man 9.00, Deadpool 26.00, Erlich 6.99, Predator 0.99, Interplanetary Batman 5.00, Kramer Golf 2.25, Kramer Good Cop 4.50, Okoye 3.50, Pajama Jack 2.50, Snoopy 11.00. Total US$76.72 x 1.4383 = A$110.34. Divided by 1.198 = A$92.10, rounded down to $90. Flip: likely resale is the median sales added up, US$230.40 x 1.4383 = A$331. Less eBay AU fees of about 13.4% plus A$0.30 per order x 11, about A$48. Buyers pay postage, packaging about A$2 x 11 = A$22. Net about A$261, divided by 2.396 = A$108.9, rounded down to $105. That is why the researcher's A$235 total undervalued a lot whose boxes look undamaged. I replaced them with dated single new-in-box sales from the same pages, filed as SOLD. Left out of the figures: chase, Target, FYE, Amazon and NYCC-only versions, invisible, red and chrome variants, multi-figure sets, damaged or 'not mint' boxes, and loose figures.
